Subject: Trial integration action grid + success criteria

Thanks again for the time today — great first discussion. Quick recap and a proposed lightweight trial action grid so we can get your engineering team into a short evaluation sprint next week. Please confirm owners/dates and any missing success criteria.

TL;DR (ask):
- Trial window: 2 weeks (staging traffic / synthetic + small production slice)
- Success criteria: functional acceptance, latency and cost targets, and qualitative output checks
- Kickoff: proposed Mon Nov 8, engineering sync (30m)

Scope (proposed):
- Core routes: text generation (streaming + non-streaming), embeddings for similarity search, and one tool-calling webhook for order-enrichment flow.
- Integration: Redwood JS SDK -> point to sandbox API keys; optional direct REST routes for server-side services.
- Observability: per-request token accounting and 95th percentile latency tracing in Redwood Console.

Draft success criteria (please edit):
1) Functional: demo flow succeeds end-to-end for 500 synthetic transactions with <= 5% regeneration rate (quality metric).
2) Latency: 95th percentile < 200ms for generation baseline on your staging traces (avg request length ~120 tokens).
3) Embeddings: top-3 recall >= 85% on your seed prompt set (we'll run a small evaluation harness).
4) Cost: projected per-1k request token cost within the target you outlined (we'll provide model/quantization options).
5) Security/compliance: data retention and audit logging documented; SOC2 evidence where required.

Owners & immediate asks:
- Jasmine Liu (me): overall trial owner / kickoff coordination / success criteria finalization
- Dev Patel: technical lead for SDK/API handoff, streaming & tool-calling tests
- Marissa Cole: CSM — scheduling, procurement touchpoints, acceptance signoff
- Ledgerly: Priya / Evan confirm internal test owners and required compliance checklist items

Kickoff cadence (proposed):
- Nov 8: 30m engineering kickoff — align endpoints, keys, and access
- Nov 9–10: baseline integration and one streaming smoke test
- Nov 11–20: acceptance run + evaluation harness
- Nov 21: acceptance review and next-step decision

Attachments: redwood-demo-sample-payloads.json (sample requests), ledgerly-system-diagram.png (referenced), po-templates.pdf (procurement stub).
Drive link with trial plan & eval harness: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-ledgerly-trial-plan

Open questions for Ledgerly: please confirm the staging endpoint hostnames and whether you prefer SDK-based auth or short-lived tokens delegated from your backend. Also flag any IP whitelisting / egress constraints.

Thanks — looking forward to your confirmation.

—
Jasmine Liu
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Cheers,

Thanks Evan — answers inline and a short technical playbook for the integration.

1) API routes (recommended starting set)
- POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate : synchronous generation (JSON response)
- POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream : streaming generation (server-sent events / chunked transfer; each chunk contains a partial token or token group)
- POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings : embeddings (batchable up to 256 inputs)
- POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/tool-call : tool-calling webhook flow (Redwood will POST to your callback with function call payload)

2) Streaming semantics
- We send chunk-per-token by default; SDKs offer buffered chunk groups to reduce socket chatter. For Lambda clients we recommend buffered groups (~8–16 tokens) to balance latency and open connections.

3) Tool-calling payloads & limits
- Tool call payload max: 128 KB (request body) — includes order_id and enrichment context. If you expect larger payloads, send a pointer (S3 presigned) instead.

4) Auth & keys
- For the trial, use sandbox API keys we will provision. Key rotation is supported; we can also issue short-lived delegated tokens if you prefer server-side delegation.

5) SDK steps (JS quick-start)
- npm install @redwood/inference@0.9.1
- const client = new RedwoodClient({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_KEY });
- client.generate({ model: 'redwood-small', prompt, max_tokens: 200, stream: true });
- For tool-calling: define tools in the SDK and register a callback URL in the Console; Redwood will POST a function_call event with name + args JSON.

6) Observability hooks
- Add the request_id header from Redwood to your logs; we will correlate token usage and traces in the Console.
- We will provide a shared dashboard link for the trial: per-route latency, token breakdown, and error traces.

7) Attachments & artifacts
- Attached: redwood-integration-sdk-v0.9.1.tgz (SDK tarball), redwood-demo-sample-payloads.json (examples), po-templates.pdf (procurement).

If this looks good I can draft a short terminal-ready checklist for your engineers to get started (keys, firewall, sample call).

—
Dev Patel
Senior Backend Engineer | Redwood Inference
